title: Rum truffles
subtitle: Rich dark ganache rolled in cocoa powder with a measure of dark rum
excerpt: Dark chocolate ganache set firm, rolled into balls, and coated in cocoa powder with a generous measure of dark rum stirred through. One of the simplest confections to make and one of the most rewarding. They set in the fridge, keep for a week, and improve with a day's rest.
sourceNotes: Chocolate rum truffles are a well-established confectionery standard, associated with the French chocolaterie tradition. The dark ganache and rum combination appears across British and French home confectionery.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze on a tray, then box. Defrost overnight in the fridge. Dust with fresh cocoa before serving.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make 3 to 4 days ahead. The rum flavour deepens with time.

glossaryTerms.definition: A confection of set ganache rolled into a ball and coated in cocoa powder, chocolate, or crushed nuts. Named for its resemblance to the underground fungi.

content.text: are made from a firm dark ganache set in the fridge, scooped, rolled, and dusted with cocoa. The rum should be present but not overpowering; dark rum works better than white because its oak and molasses notes echo the dark chocolate.

Place the finely chopped chocolate in a bowl. Bring the cream to a bare simmer over medium heat. Pour over the chocolate and leave for 1 minute. Stir from the centre outward until smooth. Add the butter and stir until glossy. Stir in the rum. Pour into a shallow dish and refrigerate for 2 hours until firm.

Sift the cocoa powder onto a flat plate. Using a melon baller or a small teaspoon, scoop small rounds of the set ganache. Roll quickly between cold palms into a ball, the ganache softens in warm hands, so work fast and chill your hands under cold water between rounds if needed. Roll immediately in the cocoa powder and place on a lined tray. Refrigerate until serving.
Serve at room temperature rather than from the fridge; the ganache softens slightly and the rum flavour opens up.
